governanceNotes: D1 batch 79 (2026-09-27): two bounded association edges authored - rickets to seizure-disorder (rank 1) and rickets to loss-of-teeth (rank 2) - both classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, and mechanismCategory METABOLIC_OR_NUTRITIONAL on both, reflecting that the two downstream tissues are consequences of one calcium and phosphate substrate deficit rather than of two independent processes. The edges rest on disjoint sources this batch (deliberately no within-batch shared-source provenance while the CRG redundancy-semantics question stands at eleven accumulated examples): the seizure-disorder edge on the 2025 case report of an eight-month-old breastfed boy with three generalised tonic seizures, total calcium 6.8 mg/dL, ionised calcium 0.91 mmol/L, 25-hydroxyvitamin D 3.5 ng/mL, and no further seizures after correction (PMID 41552144), the 2004 emergency-department three-case series presenting with fracture, tetany, and hypocalcaemic seizures (PMID 14758313), and the 2013 Olmsted County population study (hypocalcaemia or tetany in 2 of 17 nutritional cases; incidence rising to 24.1 per 100,000 in children under three, PMID 23374621); the loss-of-teeth edge on the 2026 case report of generalized permanent-dentition enamel hypoplasia with an unaffected primary dentition as a temporal control (PMID 42505708), the 2014 two-patient report of serious subsequent tooth decay (PMID 24616355), and the 2018 comparative cohort (enamel hypoplasia in 5 of 6 adults with vitamin-D-dependent rickets type 1A versus 1 of 25 with X-linked hypophosphatemia, P<0.001, PMID 28608052). Limits carried openly: the seizure edge names respiratory alkalosis and intercurrent febrile illness as cofactors in the strongest anchor and states that seizure cessation with repletion indicates a reversible metabolic rather than structural mechanism; the dental edge states that the comparative anchor describes a rare inherited subtype rather than nutritional rickets and that no anchor quantifies tooth loss. The osteomalacia, osteoporosis, osteopenia, and stress-fractures propositions are withheld on the record as manifestation-identity, shared-substrate, or duplicate-scope items, and the growth-failure, developmental-delay, and dilated-cardiomyopathy gaps are recorded as catalog-gap continuations.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Nutritional rickets presents with hypocalcaemic tetany and seizures across emergency-department and population series: the 2025 case report describes a previously healthy exclusively breastfed eight-month-old boy who developed three episodes of generalised tonic seizures initially attributed to an upper respiratory infection, in whom workup revealed total calcium of 6.8 mg/dL, ionised calcium of 0.91 mmol/L, 25-hydroxyvitamin D of 3.5 ng/mL, low phosphate, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and high parathyroid hormone - all indicative of nutritional rickets - with mild respiratory alkalosis identified as a further contributor to the decline in ionised calcium and no further seizures after correction of the hypocalcaemia (PMID 41552144); the 2004 emergency-department report of three children with rickets presents them with a fracture concerning for child abuse, tetany, and hypocalcaemic seizures, stating that in all cases laboratory and radiographic evaluations were consistent with nutritional rickets and their symptoms resolved with appropriate treatment (PMID 14758313); and the 2013 population-based Olmsted County study of 23 children with radiographic evidence of rickets, 17 of them nutritional, reports a clinical presentation including poor growth (n=12), leg deformity (n=8), motor delay (n=5), leg pain (n=3), weakness (n=3), and hypocalcaemia or tetany (n=2), with the incidence of nutritional rickets in children under three rising from 0 to 24.1 per 100,000 across four decades (P=0.003) (PMID 23374621); recorded as documented association only with the anchor-class limits carried openly - the strongest anchor is a single infant case report, the emergency-department report is a three-case series, and the population anchor records only two of seventeen children with hypocalcaemia or tetany, so the seizures are a rare complication of a rare condition and the series cannot support an incidence estimate.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of seizure disorder is established for any individual: the located anchors are one case report, one three-case series, and one population study in which only two of seventeen nutritional cases had hypocalcaemia or tetany, the seizures in the case report were febrile with a concurrent respiratory alkalosis that the authors themselves identify as contributing to the ionised-calcium decline, and the condition is a metabolic derangement that resolves with repletion rather than a structural epilepsy - the two case-report anchors report complete seizure cessation after calcium correction, which is a hallmark of the metabolic rather than the epileptic mechanism; individual claims require dated seizure history with semiology, dated serum calcium, ionised calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and parathyroid hormone values demonstrating the hypocalcaemic mechanism, and exclusion of febrile seizure, structural epilepsy, and alternative hypocalcaemic causes.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Vitamin D deficiency with dietary calcium deprivation lowers ionised serum calcium - the calcium-deprivation spectrum the 2017 review describes as having a hypocalcaemic tier comprising seizures, tetany, and dilated cardiomyopathy - so that neuronal membrane excitability rises and a susceptible infant or child seizes; the route the case and emergency-department anchors document directly, but whether the rickets produced any individual's seizure disorder remains hypothesized until the hypocalcaemic biochemistry and the seizure semiology are dated together.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at case-report, case-series, and population-based-incidence class following the metabolic-complication convention (the registered chronic-kidney-disease mineral-bone-disorder and hyperparathyroidism windows own their skeletal and biochemical routes with sources left untouched per ME-29): the case-report anchor documents the complete causal chain from breastfed infant through documented hypocalcaemia and severe vitamin D deficiency to generalised tonic seizures that stopped entirely after calcium correction (PMID 41552144), the emergency-department anchor establishes that tetany and hypocalcaemic seizures are recognised rickets presentations (PMID 14758313), and the population anchor supplies the only located incidence denominator and the frequency of the hypocalcaemic presentation at 2 of 17 nutritional cases (PMID 23374621); because the located evidence is one case, three cases, and a two-of-seventeen presentation frequency in a rising-incidence population, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with the anchor class and the rarity of the complication stated, and routes individual claims through dated hypocalcaemic biochemistry with febrile and structural causes excluded.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The strongest located anchor is a single infant case report, the emergency-department anchor is a three-case series, and the population anchor records hypocalcaemia or tetany in only 2 of 17 nutritional rickets cases, so no incidence of seizure as a rickets complication can be estimated; the case-report anchor's seizures were febrile with a concurrent respiratory alkalosis the authors identify as an additional contributor to the ionised-calcium decline, so the trigger is not attributable to rickets alone; no located anchor separates rickets-related hypocalcaemic seizures from structural or febrile epilepsy in a cohort; the population anchor's diagnostic code set included tetany and hypocalcaemic seizure by design, which inflates the identified presentation count relative to incidental detection.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Febrile seizure from concurrent intercurrent infection, present in the strongest case anchor
Respiratory alkalosis lowering ionised calcium independently, the cofactor the case anchor names
Structural or genetic epilepsy presenting coincidentally in a child with nutritional deficiency
Other hypocalcaemic causes including hypomagnesemia, pancreatitis, and citrate transfusion

evidenceGaps: The strongest located anchor is a single infant case report, the emergency-department anchor is a three-case series, and the population anchor records hypocalcaemia or tetany in only 2 of 17 nutritional rickets cases, so no incidence of seizure as a rickets complication can be estimated; the case-report anchor's seizures were febrile with a concurrent respiratory alkalosis the authors identify as an additional contributor to the ionised-calcium decline, so the trigger is not attributable to rickets alone; no located anchor separates rickets-related hypocalcaemic seizures from structural or febrile epilepsy in a cohort; the population anchor's diagnostic code set included tetany and hypocalcaemic seizure by design, which inflates the identified presentation count relative to incidental detection.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the two case anchors document the full mechanistic chain and its reversibility with correction, and the population anchor supplies a denominator showing the complication is uncommon; the conservative framing names the rarity, the febrile and alkalosis cofactors, and the resolvable-metabolic rather than structural character, so a reader sees the recognised presentation without inferring an epilepsy link.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Rickets affects the developing dentition because enamel mineralisation shares the calcium and phosphate availability that is compromised in the disease, and the located evidence documents enamel hypoplasia, enamel defects, and consequent tooth destruction: the 2026 case report describes a 6-year-9-month-old boy diagnosed with vitamin D deficiency rickets at 2 years 5 months who at dental referral had generalized discoloration and morphological abnormality of multiple permanent teeth, with generalized enamel hypoplasia of the permanent incisors and first molars showing yellow-brown discoloration, rough enamel surfaces, morphological irregularities, and attrition, while the primary dentition was unaffected, and panoramic radiography demonstrated generalized crown malformation of both erupted and unerupted permanent teeth (PMID 42505708); the 2014 report of two young girls with rickets in early childhood documents that both suffered subsequent serious tooth decay (PMID 24616355); and the 2018 comparison of 10 patients with vitamin-D-dependent rickets type 1A against 49 adult controls and 30 patients with X-linked hypophosphatemia reports enamel hypoplasia of several incisors and/or canines in five of six adults with vitamin-D-dependent rickets versus one of 25 with X-linked hypophosphatemia (P<0.001) and several first molars affected in three of four versus none of 16 (P=0.004), with endodontically affected teeth in five of seven and 24 of 30 respectively, concluding the dental aberration of vitamin-D-dependent rickets aligns with nutritional rickets and that low availability of both calcium and phosphate during enamel formation is critical (PMID 28608052); recorded as documented association only with the anchor-class limits carried openly - the strongest clinical anchor is a single patient, the decay anchor is a two-patient report, and the comparison anchor is a rare inherited subtype rather than nutritional rickets, so the evidence establishes the dentitional consequence while the population magnitude remains unquantified.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of tooth loss is established for any individual: all three anchors are small (one patient, two patients, and a rare inherited subtype cohort of ten) and none reports a rate of tooth extraction or edentulism attributable to rickets, the primary dentition is explicitly unaffected in the strongest anchor so the dental enamelation window must fall before the child is roughly eight years old, and the two inherited and nutritional pathways differ in phosphate availability so the comparison anchor's contrast with X-linked hypophosphatemia identifies a distinct phenotype rather than a general rickets effect; individual claims require dated rickets diagnosis with calcium, phosphate, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and parathyroid hormone values, dated dental and radiographic charting of the affected dentition, and exclusion of other causes of enamel hypoplasia and early childhood caries.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Systemic calcium and phosphate deprivation during the mineralisation window of permanent-tooth formation - the route the comparison anchor names when it concludes that low availability of both calcium and phosphate is critical in periods of enamel formation - leaves enamel hypoplastic and hypomineralised, producing rough, discoloured surfaces that wear and permit early destructive caries, so the dentition is compromised by the same substrate deficit that produces the skeletal findings, but whether the deficiency produced any individual's tooth loss remains hypothesized until the rickets and dental findings are dated to a shared mineralisation window.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at case-report, two-patient-case-report, and comparative-cohort class following the systemic-to-oral manifestation convention (the registered kidney-stones and oral-cancer windows own their dental and oral routes with sources left untouched per ME-29): the case-report anchor documents generalized permanent-dentition enamel hypoplasia with attrition and crown malformation following rickets diagnosed at 2 years 5 months, with the primary dentition spared as a temporal control (PMID 42505708), the two-patient anchor documents serious subsequent tooth decay (PMID 24616355), and the comparative-cohort anchor quantifies enamel hypoplasia in five of six adults with a vitamin-D-dependent subtype against one of 25 with X-linked hypophosphatemia and attributes the pattern to combined calcium and phosphate unavailability during enamel formation (PMID 28608052); because all three anchors are small and one describes a rare inherited subtype rather than the nutritional presentation, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with those limits stated and routes individual claims through dated rickets biochemistry with the mineralisation window established.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The strongest clinical anchor is a single 6-year-9-month-old patient and the decay anchor is a two-patient report, so no rate of tooth loss or extraction attributable to rickets can be estimated; the comparative anchor describes vitamin-D-dependent rickets type 1A, a rare inherited subtype, and explicitly contrasts it with X-linked hypophosphatemia rather than sampling nutritional rickets; no located anchor reports edentulism, prosthesis use, or a longitudinal dental-outcome measure; the primary dentition is unaffected in the strongest anchor, so the route is bounded to the permanent-tooth mineralisation window and cannot be generalised to earlier tooth loss.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Other causes of developmental enamel hypoplasia including trauma, infection, and fluoride excess during the same window
Early childhood caries from feeding practices, diet, and oral hygiene independent of mineralisation status
X-linked hypophosphatemia or other inherited phosphate-wasting rickets, a distinct phenotype the comparative anchor separates explicitly
Coexisting systemic disease or medication affecting calcium and phosphate availability

evidenceGaps: The strongest clinical anchor is a single 6-year-9-month-old patient and the decay anchor is a two-patient report, so no rate of tooth loss or extraction attributable to rickets can be estimated; the comparative anchor describes vitamin-D-dependent rickets type 1A, a rare inherited subtype, and explicitly contrasts it with X-linked hypophosphatemia rather than sampling nutritional rickets; no located anchor reports edentulism, prosthesis use, or a longitudinal dental-outcome measure; the primary dentition is unaffected in the strongest anchor, so the route is bounded to the permanent-tooth mineralisation window and cannot be generalised to earlier tooth loss.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the dentition is a documented downstream tissue of the same mineralisation deficit, the strongest anchor contains a built-in temporal control in the unaffected primary dentition, and the comparative anchor quantifies the defect against a control group; the conservative framing states the small anchor sizes, the inherited-subtype mismatch in the comparative anchor, and the unquantified tooth-loss magnitude, so the dentitional consequence is visible without inferring a population rate.
